propositional-logic.definition:
命题逻辑研究**命题公式**。原子命题 $p, q, r, \dots$ 是最简单、不再分解的陈述；**联结词** $
eg$（否定）、$\wedge$（合取）、$\vee$（析取）、$	o$（蕴含）、$\leftrightarrow$（等值）把较短公式逐层拼成复合公式。联结词的含义完全由**真值表**规定，与命题的实际内容无关：$p	o q$ 只在前件 $p$ 真、结论 $q$ 假时为假，**其余情形（包括 $p$ 为假的全部情形）都为真**——「前件假则蕴含式为真」是最常被写错的一条，它正是等值式 $p	o q\Leftrightarrow
eg p\vee q$ 的直接体现。给定一组**真值赋值**（给每个原子命题指定真或假），公式的真值被唯一确定；含 $n$ 个不同原子命题的公式，真值表恰有 $2^n$ 行。

按真值表把公式分成三类：在**一切**赋值下都为真的叫**重言式**（永真式），如 $p\vee
eg p$；在一切赋值下都为假的叫**矛盾式**（永假式，也称不可满足式），如 $p\wedge
eg p$；**至少存在一组**赋值使其为真的叫**可满足式**。三类的关系要理清：重言式都可满足，可满足式未必重言；矛盾式恰是不可满足式；而 $\varphi$ 是重言式当且仅当 $
eg\varphi$ 不可满足。真值表是最朴素的判决程序：它总能在 $2^n$ 行内给出答案，但规模随 $n$ 指数增长——这提醒我们「判定」与「找证明」是两条不同的路（见 formal-proof-systems）。

两个公式**等值**（记 $\Leftrightarrow$）指真值表逐行相同；**等值演算**就是在等值定律——德摩根律、双重否定、分配律、蕴含律 $p	o q\Leftrightarrow
eg p\vee q$、逆否律 $p	o q\Leftrightarrow
eg q	o
eg p$ 等——之下的符号变形。这里要区分对象语言里的联结词 $\leftrightarrow$（本身有真值表）与元语言里的 $\Leftrightarrow$（断言两式等值，不是公式的一部分）。等值变形保持一切真值，因此可以像代数化简一样把公式化成范式来简化电路或核对论证。反面要牢记：$p	o q$ 与它的逆命题 $q	o p$、否命题 $
eg p	o
eg q$ 都**不等值**，只有逆否命题 $
eg q	o
eg p$ 才与原式等值。

五个联结词并不互相独立：$\{
eg,\wedge,\vee\}$ 已是**完备联结词集**，能表达一切真值函数；$\{
eg,	o\}$ 也完备（$\wedge$、$\vee$ 可由二者定义）；$n$ 个变元的真值函数共有 $2^{2^n}$ 个（两个变元恰有 16 个），所以「完备集」是把无穷张真值表压进有限符号的办法。反过来，$\{\wedge,\vee\}$ 不完备（造不出否定），$\{	o\}$ 单独更不行；而**与非**（NAND，$\uparrow$）与**或非**（NOR，$\downarrow$）各自单独就是完备集（Sheffer 竖线）——数字电路只用一种逻辑门就能搭建全部组合逻辑，正是这一事实的工程版本。联结词完备性也是后面用极少数公理模式刻画全部重言式的前提（见 formal-proof-systems、soundness-completeness）。
propositional-logic.definitionEn:
Propositional logic studies **propositional formulas**. Atomic propositions $p, q, r, \dots$ are the simplest indecomposable statements; the **connectives** $
eg$ (negation), $\wedge$ (conjunction), $\vee$ (disjunction), $	o$ (implication) and $\leftrightarrow$ (equivalence) combine shorter formulas into compound ones. Their meaning is fixed entirely by **truth tables**, independent of subject matter: $p	o q$ is false only when the antecedent $p$ is true and the consequent $q$ is false, and **true in every other case—including all cases where $p$ is false**. That vacuous truth is the most frequently misstated line, and it is exactly the equivalence $p	o q\Leftrightarrow
eg p\vee q$. Once a **truth assignment** maps each atomic proposition to true or false, the formula's truth value is determined; a formula with $n$ distinct atoms has a truth table of exactly $2^n$ rows.

Truth tables sort formulas into three classes: **tautologies** (true under every assignment), such as $p\vee
eg p$; **contradictions** (false under every assignment, i.e. unsatisfiable), such as $p\wedge
eg p$; and **satisfiable formulas** (true under at least one assignment). The relationships matter: tautologies are satisfiable, satisfiable formulas need not be tautologies, contradictions are exactly the unsatisfiable formulas, and $\varphi$ is a tautology iff $
eg\varphi$ is unsatisfiable. Truth tables are the simplest decision procedure: they always answer within $2^n$ rows but grow exponentially—a reminder that deciding differs from proving (see formal-proof-systems).

Two formulas are **equivalent** (written $\Leftrightarrow$) when their truth tables agree row by row; **equational reasoning** rewrites formulas using equivalence laws—De Morgan, double negation, distributivity, the implication law $p	o q\Leftrightarrow
eg p\vee q$ and contraposition $p	o q\Leftrightarrow
eg q	o
eg p$. Keep apart the object-language connective $\leftrightarrow$ (which itself has a truth table) and the metalanguage symbol $\Leftrightarrow$ (the assertion that two formulas are equivalent, not part of any formula). Equivalence transformations preserve all truth values, so formulas can be simplified into normal forms much like algebraic expressions. Beware the converse and the inverse: $p	o q$ is **not** equivalent to $q	o p$ nor to $
eg p	o
eg q$; only the contrapositive $
eg q	o
eg p$ matches.

The five connectives are not independent: $\{
eg,\wedge,\vee\}$ is **functionally complete**, expressing every truth function; $\{
eg,	o\}$ is complete too (since $\wedge$, $\vee$ are definable from them); there are $2^{2^n}$ truth functions of $n$ variables (16 binary ones), so a complete set compresses all truth tables into finitely many symbols. By contrast $\{\wedge,\vee\}$ is not complete (it cannot express negation at all), and neither is $\{	o\}$ alone; but **NAND** ($\uparrow$) and **NOR** ($\downarrow$) each form a one-element complete set (Sheffer strokes)—the theoretical fact behind building all digital logic from a single gate type. Completeness of connectives also underlies describing all tautologies by a few axiom schemata (see formal-proof-systems, soundness-completeness).

formulas.noteEn: Excluded middle and contradiction: 1 and 0 stand for constantly true and constantly false; the prototypes of tautology and contradiction.

properties: 对每一组真值赋值，每个命题公式恰有一个真值；因此等值、重言、矛盾、可满足都可由枚举 2ⁿ 行判定——命题逻辑的判定问题是可解的。
三类公式互为否定地成对：φ 重言 ⟺ ¬φ 不可满足；φ 矛盾 ⟺ ¬φ 重言；既非重言又非矛盾的公式（偶然式）与它的否定都可满足。
替换定理：若 A ⇔ B，则在任何公式中把子公式 A 替换为 B，所得公式与原公式等值——这是等值演算「步步保真」的根据。
联结词完备性是对表达能力的精确刻画：{¬,∧,∨}、{¬,→}、{↑}、{↓} 完备；{∧,∨} 不完备，因为它只能生成单调真值函数，无法实现否定。
蕴含不可交换：(p→q)→(q→p) 不是重言式（p 假、q 真时整个蕴含着取假值）；等值箭头 ↔ 与单方向箭头 → 有本质区别。
propertiesEn: Under each truth assignment every formula has exactly one truth value; equivalence, tautologicity, contradictoriness and satisfiability are all decidable by enumerating the 2ⁿ rows—propositional logic is decidable.
The three classes come in negated pairs: φ is a tautology iff ¬φ is unsatisfiable, and φ is a contradiction iff ¬φ is a tautology; a contingency (neither) is satisfiable together with its negation.
Substitution theorem: if A ⇔ B, replacing a subformula A by B inside any formula yields an equivalent formula—this is what makes equational reasoning sound step by step.
Functional completeness measures expressive power precisely: {¬,∧,∨}, {¬,→}, {↑} and {↓} are complete, while {∧,∨} is not—it generates only monotone truth functions and can never express negation.
Implication does not commute: (p→q)→(q→p) is not a tautology (it fails when p is false and q is true); the biconditional ↔ and the one-way arrow → are genuinely different connectives.

用真值表判断 $\varphi=(p	o q)\vee(q	o p)$ 是否重言式；再验证等值式 $
eg(p	o q)\Leftrightarrow p\wedge
eg q$ 与 $p	o q\Leftrightarrow

examples.solution:
按 $(p,q)=(1,1),(1,0),(0,1),(0,0)$ 四行枚举。第一式：$p	o q$ 取 $1,0,1,1$，$q	o p$ 取 $1,1,0,1$，逐行取析取得 $1,1,1,1$——$\varphi$ 对全部四组赋值都为真，是**重言式**（含义：任意两个命题间的蕴含至少有一个方向成立）。等值核对：$
eg(p	o q)$ 与 $p\wedge
eg q$ 都只在 $(1,0)$ 行为真，其余为假，逐行相同；$p	o q$ 与 $
eg q	o
eg p$ 的真值行同为 $1,0,1,1$，完全一致。而 $(p	o q)	o(q	o p)$ 在 $(0,1)$ 行：前件 $p	o q=1$、后件 $q	o p=0$，整个蕴含式取 $0$，故不是重言式——蕴含方向不能交换。以上四类核对由程序枚举 $2^2=4$ 组赋值逐项验证，无一行例外。

predicate-logic.definition:
谓词逻辑在命题逻辑之上引入**个体变元** $x, y, z, \dots$、常元、函数符号与谓词（关系）符号：项由变元与函数符号生成，把谓词作用在项上得到**原子公式**（如 $R(x,y)$、$x<y$），再用 $
eg,\wedge,\vee,	o$ 和**量词** $ orall$（全称，「对每一个」）、$\exists$（存在，「至少有一个」）逐层构造合式公式。量词紧接的公式是它的**辖域**；变元的出现分两类：位于该变元量词辖域之内并被它约束的叫**约束出现**，否则叫**自由出现**。例如 $\exists y\,(y>x)$ 中 $y$ 约束、$x$ 自由，整个公式其实是关于 $x$ 的一个条件。没有自由变元的公式叫**闭公式**（句子），它直接具有真假；约束变元可以在不与其他变元冲突的前提下改名，公式含义不变。

语义一侧：一个**结构（解释）**给出论域 $D$ 以及各常元、函数符号、谓词符号的指称；**赋值**把自由变元映到 $D$ 中的元素。真值定义为：$ orall x\,\varphi$ 为真当且仅当对 $D$ 中**每个**元素 $a$，把 $x$ 取作 $a$ 时 $\varphi$ 为真；$\exists x\,\varphi$ 为真当且仅当**存在**至少一个 $a$ 使 $\varphi$ 为真。因此谓词逻辑的「真」总是相对于结构（与赋值）的：公式**可满足**指存在结构（与赋值）使其真，**逻辑有效（永真）**指在一切结构中都被满足。对命题逻辑来说，「所有赋值」换成了「所有结构」，判定难度随之剧增。全称断言一切、存在许诺一个——两种量词的分工是全部推理规则的源头。

否定一个量化公式的规则是**换量词、否结论**：$
eg orall x\,\varphi\Leftrightarrow\exists x\,
eg\varphi$（「不是所有都对」＝「存在一个反例」），$
eg\exists x\,\varphi\Leftrightarrow orall x\,
eg\varphi$（「不存在」＝「全部都无」）。**方向绝不能写反**：$
eg orall$ 变成 $\exists
eg$、$
eg\exists$ 变成 $ orall
eg$；多层量词由外向内逐层外推，如 $
eg orall\varepsilon\exists\delta(\dots)\Leftrightarrow\exists\varepsilon orall\delta\,
eg(\dots)$，且「否结论」时要把结论内部的等号、不等号一并翻转。另两个易错点：量词与 $\vee$、$\wedge$ 没有无条件的分配律——$ orall x(P\wedge Q)\Leftrightarrow orall xP\wedge orall xQ$ 与 $\exists x(P\vee Q)\Leftrightarrow\exists xP\vee\exists xQ$ 双向成立，但 $ orall x(P\vee Q)$ 只能由 $ orall xP\vee orall xQ$ 单向推出（反向不成立：每一点各有一个析取项成立，未必有同一点对所有点成立）；同理 $\exists xP\wedge\exists xQ$ 推不出 $\exists x(P\wedge Q)$。

同种量词可以交换（$ orall x orall y\,\varphi\Leftrightarrow orall y orall x\,\varphi$），但 $ orall x\exists y\,\varphi$ 与 $\exists y orall x\,\varphi$ 一般**不等值**：$\exists y$ 是否在 $ orall x$ 之内，决定 $y$ 能否随 $x$ 变化。经典例子：在自然数中 $ orall x\exists y\,(y>x)$ 为真（每个 $x$ 都有更大的 $y=x+1$），而 $\exists y orall x\,(y>x)$ 为假（任何 $y$ 都要面对 $x=y$）。分析里「连续」与「一致连续」的差别同源：逐点连续是 $ orall x orall\varepsilon\exists\delta orall y(\dots)$，$\delta$ 可以依赖点 $x$；一致连续把 $\exists\delta$ 提到 $ orall x$ 之前，$\delta$ 必须对全部点统一。代入公式时还要避免**变量捕获**：把含 $y$ 的项代入 $\exists y\,(y>x)$ 中的 $x$，若直接替换得 $\exists y\,(y>y)$（在把 > 解释为通常严格序时为假），$y$ 被量词「吃掉」，含义完全变了；正确做法是先把约束变元换名，得 $\exists z\,(z>y)$。
predicate-logic.definitionEn:
Predicate logic adds to propositional logic **individual variables** $x, y, z, \dots$, constants, function symbols and predicate (relation) symbols. Terms are built from variables and function symbols; applying a predicate to terms yields **atomic formulas** (like $R(x,y)$ or $x<y$), which are combined by $\neg,\wedge,\vee,\to$ and the **quantifiers** $\forall$ (for all) and $\exists$ (there exists) into well-formed formulas. The formula immediately following a quantifier is its **scope**; an occurrence of a variable inside the scope of a quantifier governing that variable is **bound**, otherwise **free**. In $\exists y\,(y>x)$, $y$ is bound and $x$ is free—the formula is really a condition about $x$. Formulas without free variables are **closed formulas** (sentences) with definite truth values; bound variables may be renamed without changing meaning.

Semantics: a **structure (interpretation)** provides a domain $D$ together with interpretations of the constants, function symbols and predicates; an **assignment** maps free variables into $D$. Truth is defined by: $\forall x\,\varphi$ is true iff $\varphi$ is true when $x$ is set to **every** element of $D$; $\exists x\,\varphi$ is true iff there is **at least one** element making $\varphi$ true. Hence truth in predicate logic is always relative to a structure (and assignment): a formula is **satisfiable** if some structure satisfies it and **valid** (logically true) if every structure does. Compared with propositional logic, every assignment has been replaced by every structure, which makes deciding validity dramatically harder. Universal quantifiers claim everything, existential quantifiers promise one element—this division is the source of all quantifier rules.

Negating a quantified formula means **swap the quantifier, negate the conclusion**: $\neg\forall x\,\varphi\Leftrightarrow\exists x\,\neg\varphi$ (not all equals there is a counterexample) and $\neg\exists x\,\varphi\Leftrightarrow\forall x\,\neg\varphi$ (there is none equals all fail). **The directions must never be reversed**, and the negation is pushed inward level by level. Two further pitfalls: quantifiers distribute over $\vee$ and $\wedge$ only one way. $\forall x(P\wedge Q)\Leftrightarrow\forall xP\wedge\forall xQ$ and $\exists x(P\vee Q)\Leftrightarrow\exists xP\vee\exists xQ$ hold both ways, but $\forall x(P\vee Q)$ follows only from $\forall xP\vee\forall xQ$ (the converse fails: at each point some disjunct holds, but not the same one everywhere); similarly $\exists xP\wedge\exists xQ$ does not imply $\exists x(P\wedge Q)$.

Quantifiers of the same kind commute ($\forall x\forall y\,\varphi\Leftrightarrow\forall y\forall x\,\varphi$), but $\forall x\exists y\,\varphi$ and $\exists y\forall x\,\varphi$ are **not** equivalent in general: whether $\exists y$ sits inside $\forall x$ decides whether $y$ may depend on $x$. The classic example: in the natural numbers $\forall x\exists y\,(y>x)$ is true (take $y=x+1$) while $\exists y\forall x\,(y>x)$ is false (any $y$ must face $x=y$). The difference between pointwise and uniform continuity is the same phenomenon: pointwise continuity reads $\forall x\forall\varepsilon\exists\delta\forall y(\dots)$, where $\delta$ may depend on the point $x$, while uniform continuity puts $\exists\delta$ before $\forall x$ so that $\delta$ works for all points at once. Finally, substitution must avoid **variable capture**: substituting a term containing $y$ for $x$ in $\exists y\,(y>x)$ naively yields $\exists y\,(y>y)$, false under the usual strict-order interpretation—the variable $y$ has been swallowed by its own quantifier. Rename the bound variable first: the correct result is $\exists z\,(z>y)$.

formulas.note: 量词否定律：换量词、否结论。¬∀ 必得 ∃¬，¬∃ 必得 ∀¬——方向写反是最经典的错误。
formulas.noteEn: Quantifier negation: swap the quantifier and negate the conclusion; ¬∀ must yield ∃¬ and ¬∃ must yield ∀¬.

formulas.latex: \forall x(\varphi\wedge\psi)\ \Leftrightarrow\ \forall x\varphi\wedge\forall x\psi,\qquad \exists x(\varphi\vee\psi)\ \Leftrightarrow\ \exists x\varphi\vee\exists x\psi
formulas.note: 同向联结词可双向分配；换成 ∨ 与 ∧ 之后只剩单向（见下条）。
formulas.noteEn: Quantifiers distribute both ways over the matching connective; over the opposite connective only one direction survives.
